verses.commentary: Listen to what the Lord says: Stand up, plead my case before the mountains; let the hills hear. Cosmic courtroom. Mountains as witnesses. God brings charges and calls creation to observe. The lawsuit (riv) begins.

Hear, mountains, the Lord's accusation; listen, everlasting foundations. The Lord has a case against his people; he lodges charges against Israel. Ancient witnesses summoned. What has stood from the beginning now listens. The defendant is named: Israel.

My people, what have I done to you? How have I burdened you? Answer me. God invites defense. The question is stunning. Has God wronged Israel? Let them explain their grievance. Silence is the only possible response.
I brought you from Egypt, redeemed you from slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. The evidence: exodus deliverance. Slavery ended. Leadership provided. History testifies to divine faithfulness.

Remember what Balak king of Moab plotted and what Balaam answered. Remember the journey from Shittim to Gilgal that you may know the Lord's righteous acts. Balaam's blessing instead of curse. The Jordan crossing. Specific memories invoked. Righteousness demonstrated through salvation.

With what shall I come before the Lord, bow before the exalted God? Shall I come with burnt offerings, with calves a year old? The response begins. What does God want? The worshiper asks. Offerings are proposed.

Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I offer my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul? Escalation. Quantity increases. Then the ultimate offer: child sacrifice. How far must one go?

He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require? To act justly, love mercy, walk humbly with your God. The answer cuts through ritual complexity. Three requirements: justice in action, mercy as disposition, humble communion with God. Micah 6:8 is the prophet's most famous verse.

Listen! The Lord is calling to the city. To fear your name is wisdom. Heed the rod and the One who appointed it. The city addressed. Fear of God equals wisdom. The rod of discipline speaks. Pay attention to what judgment teaches.

Am I still to forget your ill gotten treasures? The short ephah, which is accursed? Rhetorical question. Dishonest business practices. The ephah (a measure) cheated. God does not forget economic injustice.

Shall I acquit someone with dishonest scales, with a bag of false weights? Another rhetorical question. Fraudulent commerce. Rigged measurements. Acquittal is impossible. Justice cannot ignore injustice.
Your rich people are violent; your inhabitants are liars, their tongues speak deceitfully. Wealth linked to violence. Speech corrupted throughout society. Economic and verbal sin together.
Therefore I have begun to destroy you, to ruin you because of your sins. Judgment already underway. Present tense destruction. Sins produce consequences that have started manifesting.

You will eat but not be satisfied; your stomach will still be empty. You will store up but save nothing; what you save I will give to the sword. Covenant curses activated. Consumption without satisfaction. Accumulation without preservation. Futility cycle.

You will plant but not harvest. You will press olives but not use the oil, crush grapes but not drink the wine. Agricultural futility. Labor produces no enjoyment. The harvest taken. Covenant curses from Deuteronomy 28.

You have observed Omri's statutes and all Ahab's house practices; you have followed their traditions. Therefore I give you to ruin and your people to derision; you will bear the scorn of the nations. Northern kingdom's sins adopted by the south. Omri and Ahab's legacy embraced. Ruin and mockery result. International shame for covenant unfaithfulness.
